metadata.description: DSH plugin: after an agent's own bash or shell command, refresh the file observations it made stale, so FS_STALE_VERSION only fires on writes by others
metadata.name: dsh-fs-reobserve

paragraphs.text: DSH plugin: after an agent's own bash or shell command, refresh the file observations it made stale,
so FS_STALE_VERSION only fires on writes by others
# dsh-fs-reobserve
Ends self-inflicted stale-file errors after an agent's own shell commands.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

A DSH plugin that supplies the missing middle ground for
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-observation-policy`.
## The problem

The observation policy learns a file's version **only** from instrumented
filesystem operations (`re

ad`, `write` and `edit`), which emit
`fs/observed`. `dsh-tool-bash`, `dsh-shell` and `dsh-subprocess

-local`
contain **no reference** to that event. DSH's own documentation:
> Only instrumented filesystem operations report here; the OS is not watched.

So a session that modifies a file through bash leaves a **stale** observation,
and its very next edi

t of that file is refused with `FS_STALE_VERSION`: an
error caused entirely by the session's own act

that file is refused with `FS_STALE_VERSION`: an
error caused entirely by the session's own action.
## The three options
| | Strict | **dsh-fs-reobserve** | Disabled |

| Stale error from your *own* bash writes | fires | **gone** | gone |
| Stale error from a *third-pa

rty* writer | fires (correct) | **fires (correct)** | suppressed (unsafe) |
| `FS_NOT_OBSERVED` (rea

d before edit) | enforced | **enforced** | gone |
| Worst-case failure | wasted call | **wasted call

** | silent data loss |
| Discipline required | yes | **none** | none |
## What it does

After one of a session's own `bash`/`shell` calls settles, it re-stats the
targets **that session**

had observed and re-emits `fs/observed` at their
current state. All three transitions are covered:

- **present → present (new version)**: the command rewrote the file
- **present → absent**: the comm

and deleted the file
- **absent → present**: the command created a file a read had confirmed missing

A version is never manufactured; it comes from `ctx.fs.stat`, the only
sanctioned source.
## What it deliberately does not do

It never re-observes a change the session did not cause. A file rewritten by
cron, another agent, or

a desktop editor keeps its old observation, so the next
edit still fails with `FS_STALE_VERSION` an

d the agent is still forced to
re-read. That is the protection worth keeping.
## Configuration

Options are read from the plugin's loader entry config (the `fs-reobserve` row in your
profile's `co

rdis.patch.yml`); a `settings.yaml` section is not read. Example in
docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md.
| Key | Default | Meaning |

| `tools` | `[bash, shell]` | out-of-band tools to react to |
| `notify` | `true` | attach a notice

to the tool result so the agent knows |
| `maxNotifyPaths` | `4` | paths named before eliding |
## Install
Install from npm: `dsh plugin --profile web add @lucagiftzek/dsh-fs-reobserve`, or from GitHub: `dsh
plugin --profile web add github:lucagiftzek/dsh-fs-reobserve`.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
A local checkout works the same way: `dsh plugin --profile web add link:/absolute/path/to/dsh-fs-reo

bserve`.
Requires Node 22.5 or newer and a DSH build that ships `@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-observation-pol

icy`
(used on DSH 0.1.5 and 0.2.1). Tests: `npm test`.

The package declares `dsh.bundle`, so `dsh plugin add` puts it in `dsh.profile.bundles`
and its own
patch inserts the `fs-reobserve` entry. Do not add a second insert row by hand.

## When something goes wrong

- Ask your agent to load the **`fs-reobserve-doctor`** skill. This version does not register
it auto

matically: copy `skills/fs-reobserve-doctor` into `~/.dsh/skills/` once
(how).
- Symptom-first guide

: docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md.
- Codes and log lines: docs/ERRORS.md.
